conditions.parameterExtremes: Static count; the sample routine is straight-line, so every setting costs the same. verify.py renders FAT, COLOR and GAIN at 0 and 127 and between. Hardware: pending.
conditions.parameterModulation: Pending on hardware (the first build overran there under p-locks and scene moves). FAT and GAIN are read every block; COLOR runs a table interpolation and one division in a block where it changed. verify.py and benchmark.py move every control every block: 203 executed instructions per sample (one instance), worst 13,536 per core per block (four instances).
conditions.modeSwitching: No modes. A call boundary inside a block keeps every state and starts a new gain ramp, as the model does (verify.py). Hardware FX reselection, NONE bypass and Part changes pending; selection runs init (549 instructions) once.
conditions.maxLoad: Static: eight instances per core (FX1 and FX2 on four tracks) = 1,544 cycles/sample against 3,120 usable. Not measured on hardware.
conditions.inputConditions: verify.py: silence (also from a garbage-filled instance block), a 0.8 impulse, a step, 50 Hz-12 kHz tones, a burst and white noise at -2 dBFS and 0.22 FS, and a 60 Hz burst into a second of silence at full gain. Hardware pending.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: fatten a drum loop
steps: On a track playing a drum loop, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to FATTENER and press YES. Press FX2 to see FAT, COLOR and GAIN at the JSFX defaults.
Turn FAT up to about 80: the loop gets louder and denser as the compressor pulls the peaks in and the makeup lifts the rest.
Turn COLOR up to move the emphasis from the kick towards the snare and hats, and to harden the clip. Use GAIN to drive it harder or back off.
